title: Firmware, Bootloader and BSP Architecture

standard.family: AutoLeaP Embedded Systems Body of Knowledge

summary: Firmware architecture begins before the first application function runs. Reset state, clock and memory initialization, vector placement, language runtime setup, board configuration and driver sequencing establish the assumptions on which the rest of the product depends. Early failures need dedicated observability because normal logging, storage and networking may not yet be available.
learningObjectives: Trace execution from reset to application readiness.
Separate bootloader, BSP, HAL and driver responsibilities.
Design authenticated update, rollback and recovery behavior.
explanation: Firmware architecture begins before the first application function runs. Reset state, clock and memory initialization, vector placement, language runtime setup, board configuration and driver sequencing establish the assumptions on which the rest of the product depends. Early failures need dedicated observability because normal logging, storage and networking may not yet be available.

A bootloader selects, authenticates and activates software. A resilient design separates immutable trust code from mutable update logic, authenticates metadata and images, and records health transitions atomically. A/B or transactional activation preserves a known-good path when power is lost or the new image fails. Rollback policy must also consider security downgrade prevention and persistent-data compatibility.

A BSP binds portable software to a board: memory layout, clocks, pins, devices and power sequencing. A HAL exposes stable capabilities, while device drivers implement device behavior and OS integration. Product policy should stay above these layers. The best BSP architecture supports multiple boards through validated configuration rather than scattered conditional compilation.
whyItMatters: Boot and update failures can make otherwise correct products unserviceable.
Clear BSP and driver boundaries reduce the cost of hardware variants and vendor changes.
inputs: Board schematics and SoC startup rules
activities: Define boot metadata, slots and health checks
Allocate BSP, HAL and driver responsibilities
Create early-boot diagnostics and reset-cause handling
Test interrupted update, bad image and data migration
automotiveExample: An ECU stores immutable first-stage code, two signed application slots and a small trusted metadata area. First boot of a new image runs migration and self-tests before committing health. If the watchdog resets before commitment, the bootloader returns to the previous slot and preserves a diagnostic record for service.
commonMistakes: Marking an image successful immediately after jumping to it
Updating application data schemas without rollback compatibility
Embedding product behavior in board initialization
Ignoring bootloader and calibration version dependencies
Relying on debugger-only diagnostics during bring-up
